newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Typhoon Willie brings new havoc to central Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Willie brings new havoc to central Vietnam.

text.p: Typhoon Willie's torrential rains damaged thousands of houses and submerged huge areas of rice paddy in the central provinces of Vietnam, the country's Disaster Management Unit said in a report on Tuesday.
The unit, a joint project between the government and the United Nations Development Programme, said 56,200 households were affected in the north-central province of Nghe An alone.
The typhoon weakened to a tropical low pressure system after it landed on Sunday evening, but it nevertheless brought winds of up to 63 miles (101 km) per hour.
The Disaster Management Unit said there were no reports of deaths from the area.

Willie was the sixth tropical storm to threaten Vietnam this year. Forty-four people died and an estimated $300 million of damage was caused in seven central provinces earlier this month when a tropical storm brought heavy rains and flooding.
That took to more than 430 the number of people who have died in storms and flooding in northern and central Vietnam since the beginning of July.
